example.status: Illustrative process, not a patient outcome
example.question: “My child loves this game. What might help them take part with another child?”
steps: Bring a game your child enjoys or describe what makes it engaging. Notice the communication, movement and help already involved.
Discuss a suitable way to share a turn or express a choice. Relevant support follows that individual priority.
Ask how a family member can guide a familiar activity, and whether teacher observations would be useful with your consent.
Compare what happened with different people and support. Keep, adjust or reconsider the plan with the professional rather than assuming the activity alone proves an outcome.

stages.title: Understand abilities
stages.text: Start with strengths, everyday observations and suitable assessment. Read AbilityScore with the child’s age, context and skills.

stages.title: Plan for readiness
stages.text: Discuss what you want to make possible and agree useful priorities. Readiness views support professional judgement.

stages.title: Choose relevant support
stages.text: Bring in the therapies, educational support or health review that fit this child. Every child does not need every service.

stages.title: Practise in everyday life
stages.text: Use manageable, guided practice in meaningful routines. Family participation connects the work with daily life.

stages.title: Track and correct
stages.text: Bring relevant observations back into review. Ask what became useful, what support remains and what needs to change.

stages.title: Reassess and repeat
stages.text: Compare abilities and context over time. Continue, adapt or complete support according to the child’s needs.

stages.title: Grow independence and participation
stages.text: Keep self-sufficiency, learning, relationships and mainstream participation in view. Progress is individual.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: PinnacleAI®
pinnacleEcosystem.role: One system. Your child’s whole life.
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Ability measurement, a child-specific plan, integrated therapies, everyday practice, tracking and reassessment work toward your child’s self-sufficient, mainstream-included life.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: AbilityScore®
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Bring your child’s present abilities into a clear conversation. Measurement helps the family and professional choose meaningful goals and compare progress at review.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: 7 Readiness Indexes
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Consider what your child is ready to work toward, the support involved and the plan to discuss. Readiness connects measurement with practical decisions.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: 160 Years · Paradigm Shift
pinnacleEcosystem.role: Begin with the life we want to make possible.
pinnacleEcosystem.text: The purpose shapes the measurement, goals, therapies, home practice and review from the beginning. A useful ability matters because of the life it enables.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: Self-Sufficient
pinnacleEcosystem.role: More of everyday life, with less help.
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Choosing, communicating, getting ready and taking part in familiar routines give independence a practical meaning. Relevant support grows around your child’s own priorities.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: Mainstream
pinnacleEcosystem.role: A place in school, community and life.
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Learning alongside others, joining play and participating in everyday settings are the direction. Readiness, suitable support and family and school observations guide the journey.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: Verify
pinnacleEcosystem.role: Inspect the facts behind the confidence.
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Read original software licences, certificates, auditor reports and defined network figures. Follow each document’s scope, dates and UDIN trail directly to its source.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: Research
pinnacleEcosystem.role: Understand the science and its evaluation.
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Explore the mechanism, evidence dossier, study methods and published research. See how the system is described, what was evaluated and what each source establishes.

pinnacleEcosystem.title: Citations
pinnacleEcosystem.text: Parents, teachers, clinicians and scholars can share the relevant original source with its date and scope. Stable evidence links make the claims easier to inspect and discuss.

networkStoryPlaylists.title: AbilityScore® · our professionals explain
networkStoryPlaylists.label: How we measure
networkStoryPlaylists.question: How do we understand your child’s starting point?
networkStoryPlaylists.text: Hear practitioners describe AbilityScore®, the abilities they measure and the way they discuss progress. Bring your own questions about what a useful measurement would mean for your child.

networkStoryPlaylists.title: AbilityScore® · parents speak
networkStoryPlaylists.label: Parents explain
networkStoryPlaylists.question: What has the journey meant to other parents?
networkStoryPlaylists.text: Listen to parents speak about PinnacleAI®, AbilityScore® and their child’s journey in their own words. Notice the questions, changes and everyday priorities they choose to share.

networkStoryPlaylists.title: Our professionals’ Soul Promise
networkStoryPlaylists.label: Our promise
networkStoryPlaylists.question: What purpose brings our people together?
networkStoryPlaylists.text: Meet the people behind Pinnacle’s promise to children and families. Hear why growing abilities, participation and a wonderful life give their work its direction.

networkStoryPlaylists.title: Hear directly from families
networkStoryPlaylists.label: Families share
networkStoryPlaylists.question: What does progress look like in family life?
networkStoryPlaylists.text: Hear families describe participation, progress and the support around their child. Their stories connect the larger Pinnacle purpose with the moments that matter at home and beyond.

chapters.title: Understand your child.
chapters.purpose: Turn the life you want to make possible into an explained starting picture and a child-specific plan.
chapters.family: Bring what your child enjoys, what they can already do and the everyday priority that matters to your family. Ask what was measured, why the goal matters and how it will be reviewed.

chapters.title: Connect therapy with everyday life.
chapters.purpose: Give relevant therapies one useful direction, and help the family carry guided practice into familiar routines.
chapters.family: See a suitable activity demonstrated. Agree what fits your day, how much help to offer and what to notice. Home participation supports professional care; you are not expected to do everything alone.

chapters.title: Track. Review. Correct.
chapters.purpose: Bring what happens in the centre, at home and in relevant learning settings back into the next decision.
chapters.family: Share what your child used, where it happened, how comfortable they were and which help still mattered. Reassessment and your observations guide whether to continue, adapt or reconsider the plan.

chapters.title: Your child’s life is the purpose.
chapters.purpose: Keep growing independence, school readiness, relationships and mainstream participation in view at every stage.
chapters.family: Look beyond completing an activity. Discuss whether an ability helps your child choose, communicate, join a routine or take part with another person, and what support makes that possible.

homeParticipation.title: At the centre
homeParticipation.text: Your professional explains the goal and demonstrates suitable practice. Ask how the activity connects with the life priority you chose.

homeParticipation.title: At home
homeParticipation.text: A parent, family member or caregiver brings a manageable opportunity into play, a meal or another familiar routine. The child’s choices and comfort stay central.

homeParticipation.title: With school and caregivers
homeParticipation.text: With your consent, relevant teachers and caregivers can share observations and discuss the support that helps participation in another setting.
